prerequisites.title: Verify prerequisites
commands: sudo apt update && sudo apt install -y wget unzip

ls -la /dev/tpm*
# Expected: /dev/tpm0 or /dev/tpmrm0 (enable TPM in BIOS if absent)

install.title: Install TrustEdge
notes: Log out and back in after adding yourself to the trustedge group

tpm_provision.title: Provision TPM 2.0
commands:
cd trustedge/tools/SecureElement
unzip tpm2_tools-x86_64-{{VERSION}}.zip
unzip tpm2_tools-x86_64.zip
notes: Verify TPM path with: ls -la /dev/tpm* — substitute /dev/tpmrm0 if needed
If provisioning fails, ensure no other process is using the TPM

cert_selfsigned.title: Generate self-signed certificate
commands: trustedge certificate -a SS -g ECDSA_256 -o mydevice.pem -x mydevice.pem -da 365

run_cli.title: Run TrustEdge CLI
commands:
trustedge mqtt \
  --broker mqtt.digicert.com --port 8883 \
  --topic test/hello --message "Hello from TrustEdge" \
  --cert /etc/digicert/keystore/certs/mydevice.pem \
  --key /etc/digicert/keystore/keys/mydevice.pem

run_agent.title: Run TrustEdge agent daemon
commands: sudo systemctl enable trustedge && sudo systemctl start trustedge

pqc_demo.title: Post-Quantum (ML-DSA) demo
commands: trustedge certificate -a QS -g MLDSA_44 -o CA.pem -x CA.pem -i ca_csr.cnf -da 3651

trustedge certificate -a QS -g MLDSA_44 \
  -o server.pem -x server.pem \
  -i server_csr.cnf -da 3651 \
  -sk CA.pem -sc CA.pem
notes: PQC requires TLS 1.3 — TrustEdge enforces this automatically
